forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Halton set its 2026/27 budget with £33.9m of government-approved exceptional financial support
news_drafts.lead:
Halton Borough Council set a balanced budget for 2026/27 only with government approval of £33.9m of exceptional financial support (permission from government to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending, a last resort). The council's own self-assessment against the financial management standards set by the accountancy body CIPFA, put to its Audit and Governance Board on 30 September, says so directly: it "has set a balanced 2026/27 budget but has required approval from Government of £33.9m of Exceptional Financial Support."

The same document sets out the position beyond this year. The council's medium-term financial strategy (its financial plan, here covering five years to 2031/32) shows that "without the use of Exceptional Financial Support the Council will not be able to set a balanced budget over the 5 year term." The support therefore covers each year from 2027/28 to 2031/32 as well, not 2026/27 alone.

Government oversight runs alongside. The Corporate Overview and Improvement Board was set up in May 2026 as a six-month pilot funded by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) for councils needing this support. It includes council leaders and officers, a Local Government Association regional representative and outside specialists in local government finance. At the end of the six months, in November, its independent members must give MHCLG assurance on Halton's financial recovery plan and position. The board has met five times so far.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix B Self Assessment CIPFA Financial Management Audit and Governance Board 300926

news_drafts.headline: Halton Council faces £72m five-year budget deficit despite £29.8m savings plan
news_drafts.lead: Halton Council's five-year financial strategy, presented to the Executive Board on 17 September, forecasts a cumulative budget deficit of £72.567m over the period, even after £29.8m in planned savings. The strategy document states this is "clearly unsustainable" and warns that without exceptional financial support (emergency borrowing from government), the chief finance officer must issue a Section 114 notice (a formal warning that freezes new spending), triggering an emergency council meeting within 21 days. The council has used emergency borrowing for three consecutive years: £10m, £14.7m, and £33.873m. By 2031/32, servicing this emergency borrowing alone will cost £27.504m annually—12.7% of total council resources. A CIPFA review found the financial position "extremely fragile" and concluded the council could not stabilise without continued emergency support.

findings.headline: Adults and Children's demand growth benchmarked against statistical neighbours, comparing average and cheapest peer cost baselines
findings.detail: The board has completed dynamic assessment of demand growth for Adults and Children's services against statistical neighbour benchmarks, specifically comparing average and lowest-cost peer performance. Demand forecasting methodology linking projections to financial planning has been presented to the board. Transformation activity specifically aimed at reducing demand across Children's and Adult Services is underway.
findings.matters: Controlling demand growth is central to financial sustainability; peer councils use demand forecasting and cross-council benchmarking to inform strategies and understand cost pressures
findings.figures: Benchmarking against statistical neighbours (average and cheapest cost baselines)
findings.quote: Undertake a dynamic assessment of demand growth for Adults and Children's in the Medium Term Financial Strategy versus statistical neighbour benchmark (average and cheapest).

findings.headline: SEND deficit being actively managed through Reform Plan with detailed cost forecasting methodology and activity presented to board
findings.detail: The board has reviewed Dedicated Schools Grant deficit management with focus on the SEND Reform Plan. Completed actions include presentation of activity underway to reduce the SEND deficit and detailed methodology and assumptions for forecasting SEND-related costs. A dedicated MTFS for People Services is being developed to support financial planning in this area.
findings.matters: SEND deficits are significant financial pressures across English councils; councils managing deficits with explicit plans and transparent forecasting signal financial control
findings.figures: No specific figures on deficit size provided
findings.quote: Provide details of the activity underway to reduce the SEND deficit in line with the SEND Reform Plan. Provide further detail on the methodology and assumptions used to forecast SEND-related costs.

findings.headline: Year 1 savings delivery being monitored with strengthened oversight; Year 2 proposals developed and aligned with Management Team decisions (August 2026)
findings.detail: Enhanced governance arrangements support delivery of Year 1 savings plans. The board has developed proposals for strengthening oversight of Year 1 savings delivery and establishing explicit links between savings activity and budget performance. Year 2 savings proposals have been developed and aligned with Management Team information presented on 25 August 2026.
findings.matters: Whether councils achieve planned savings is a critical execution metric for lenders and peer finance directors assessing financial recovery credibility
findings.figures: Year 1 and Year 2 plans under board oversight; no specific amounts disclosed
findings.quote: Develop proposals for strengthening oversight of Year 1 savings delivery and demonstrating a clear link between savings activity and budget performance. Present detailed Year 2 savings proposals to the next Board meeting, aligned with the information presented to Management Team on 25 August 2026.

findings.headline: Financial Recovery Plan with alternative MTFS scenarios (central, best, worst case) due for presentation 13 October 2026
findings.detail: The council is developing a comprehensive Financial Recovery Plan including total savings proposals and alternative Medium Term Financial Strategy scenarios. The plan incorporates re-profiling of Exceptional Financial Support funding. Presentation to the board is scheduled for 13 October 2026. A dedicated MTFS for People Services covering both Children's and Adult Services is also in development.
findings.matters: The credibility of a council's forward financial plan directly informs lending decisions and peer benchmarking; scenario planning demonstrates engagement with range of outcomes
findings.quote: Develop alternative Medium Term Financial Strategy scenarios (Central, best and worst case). Including re-profiling of EFS and savings.

findings.headline: Council under Exceptional Financial Support with independent board required to assure MHCLG of financial recovery plan by end of six-month pilot (November 2026)
findings.detail: The Corporate Overview and Improvement Board was established in May 2026 as a six-month pilot initiative funded by MHCLG to support Halton, which requires Exceptional Financial Support. Independent board members are required to provide assurance to MHCLG on the council's financial recovery plan and position at the end of the initial six-month period. The board comprises council leadership, officers, and independent sector experts including the LGA Regional Representative and external members specialising in local government finance.
findings.matters: Councils receiving EFS are flagged as financially stressed; lenders and peer finance directors monitor whether councils establish governance structures and develop credible recovery plans
findings.figures: Six-month pilot period from May 2026; five board meetings held to date
findings.quote: The Board is a pilot initiative funded by Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) for an initial six months, to support Councils who require Exceptional Financial Support. At the end of the six month period, the independent Board members are required to provide assurance to MHCLG as to the Councils financial recovery plan and position.
